description: Wire the shared affection model (FEAT-001) into the frontend and backend: pet/なでる action by clicking the sprite with a per-day cap, an accessible heart gauge in StatsPanel, affection-driven chat tone (JA+EN system prompt), chat/battle-win affection bumps, legacy-save defaulting on load, and JA/EN i18n parity. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: FRONTEND load defaulting: in packages/frontend/src/state/useMonster.ts, after a monster is loaded/hatched/advanced, run normalizeAffection (from @ddm/shared) so legacy saves without affection get AFFECTION_INITIAL in the live state. Do this in the initial load path (right after `advance(loaded, now)` / before commit) so the UI always has a numeric affection. The care actions already route through the shared feed/train/sleep/clean (updated in FEAT-001), so their affection bumps flow automatically.

PET ACTION pure helpers in packages/frontend/src/ui-helpers.ts (JSX-free, unit-testable): add PET_DAILY_CAP (e.g. 5) and a localStorage-backed daily counter keyed by calendar day. Implement: `petStorageKey()` -> 'ddm.pets'; a pure `dayStamp(now: number): string` returning a YYYY-MM-DD local-date string; and pure functions `readPetRecord(raw: string | null, now): { day: string; count: number }` (parses stored JSON, resets to count 0 when the stored day !== today), `petsRemaining(record, now): number` = max(0, PET_DAILY_CAP - count for today), `canPet(record, now): boolean`, and `nextPetRecord(record, now): record` (increments count for today, resetting on a new day). Keep ALL date/count logic pure and testable; the thin localStorage read/write wrappers (guarded like readOnboarded/writeOnboarded) can live here too but the pure functions take `raw`/`record` + `now` so tests pass fixed values.

PET in useMonster.ts: expose `pet: () => Promise<void>` and `petsRemaining: number`. pet() reads the stored pet record, and if canPet is false it no-ops (optionally sets a gentle 'cap reached' state — but at minimum it must not raise affection past the cap). When allowed: optimistically apply the shared `pet(monster, now)` logic (commit -> saveMonster -> commit, mirroring runCareAction), then persist the incremented pet record via the guarded writer. Recompute petsRemaining into state so the UI can show it. Guard on busy like other actions.

CHAT affection bump in useMonster.ts: after a successful chat reply, raise affection by AFFECTION_GAIN_CHAT using the shared chat helper (from FEAT-001), commit, and persist via api.saveMonster. Keep the baby-no-chat guard (sendChat already early-returns when !stage.canChat) so babies never gain chat affection.

SPRITE pet interaction in packages/frontend/src/App.tsx: make the `.sprite-wrap` (or the sprite-bounce-layer) activatable to pet — add role="button", tabIndex={0}, an aria-label from a new i18n key (e.g. 'なでる' / 'Pet'), onClick + onKeyDown (Enter/Space) calling a handlePet that routes through the existing triggerCareFx pattern so it also plays a transient FX. Add a new CareAction-like 'pet' FX (heart 💗) OR a separate heart-pop overlay reusing the care-fx CSS conventions. Do not break the existing care FX, sleeping/dirty/hunger badges, or the speech bubble. When the daily cap is reached, petting should give no further affection (gate in handlePet via game.petsRemaining) but must not throw.

HEART FX: add a 'pet' entry to the CARE_EFFECTS map in ui-helpers.ts ({ className: 'fx-pet', emoji: '💗', durationMs: ~700 }) and extend the CareAction union to include 'pet', OR add a dedicated heart-pop descriptor. Add matching CSS in packages/frontend/src/styles.css (.care-fx.fx-pet + @keyframes) AND a prefers-reduced-motion fallback consistent with the existing care-fx reduced-motion block (fx-reduced-fade). No new runtime dependencies; audio-free.

HEART GAUGE pure helpers in ui-helpers.ts: add `affectionPercent(affection: number): number` (clamp to 0..100 against AFFECTION_MAX, non-finite -> 0, like fullnessPercent) and `affectionLevelLabel(affection, lang)` returning a localized band label (cold/neutral/warm via shared affectionBand) e.g. JA よそよそしい / ふつう / なかよし and EN Distant / Friendly / Bonded. Add unit tests for both.

HEART GAUGE UI in packages/frontend/src/components/StatsPanel.tsx: add a new stat-row near the fullness gauge that renders a heart icon (❤️, aria-hidden) + label (new i18n key stats.affection 'なつき度' / 'Affection') + a bar whose width is affectionPercent + a visible numeric value (e.g. `{pct}% ({affection}/100)`) + the band label text. Make it ACCESSIBLE and NOT color-only: give the stat-row an aria-label combining the gauge name, the percentage/value, AND the band label (mirror the fullness gauge's aria-label pattern). Read affection via affectionOf(monster) from @ddm/shared so legacy state is safe.

CHAT TONE in packages/backend/src/handlers/chat.ts buildSystemPrompt(context, lang): use context.affection + shared affectionBand to vary tone. For JA: warm band => より親しげでくだけた甘えん坊な口調; neutral => current friendly tone (KEEP the existing neutral JA lines BYTE-IDENTICAL so existing behavior is the default); cold => よそよそしく少し距離のある口調. Do the same for EN variants. The baby-no-chat branch and the lang default MUST remain intact. Default affection to AFFECTION_INITIAL when context has none (chooseChatContext already defaults it in FEAT-001). Add/adjust an extra personality line reflecting the band rather than rewriting the whole prompt, to minimize drift.

I18N: in packages/frontend/src/i18n.ts add to BOTH JA_MESSAGES and EN_MESSAGES (same keys, EN typed Record so a missing key fails the build): stats.affection (なつき度 / Affection), the three band labels (e.g. affection.cold / affection.neutral / affection.warm with よそよそしい・ふつう・なかよし and Distant / Friendly / Bonded), pet action label + aria (e.g. action.pet 'なでる' / 'Pet', action.petAria), and optionally a 'daily cap reached' hint (action.petCapReached 'きょうはもう十分なでたよ' / 'You've petted it enough for today'). Keep ALL existing keys/strings byte-identical. Prefer sourcing band labels from one place: affectionLevelLabel can read these i18n keys via t(lang, ...).

TESTS in packages/frontend/src/game-ui.test.ts (node:test, imports from ui-helpers.ts/i18n.ts only — no JSX): cover affectionPercent (0, mid, max, >max clamp, non-finite -> 0), affectionLevelLabel for each band in ja AND en, dayStamp determinism for a fixed timestamp, readPetRecord parsing + same-day vs new-day reset, petsRemaining/canPet at 0, under cap, and at cap, and nextPetRecord incrementing then resetting on a new day. Keep the pre-existing 63 frontend tests passing; count must increase.
Verify no new runtime dependency was added (no package.json dependency changes). Run the full build + both test suites.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking (or Enter/Space on) the sprite pets the monster, raises affection, plays a heart FX, and is blocked once the per-day cap (PET_DAILY_CAP) is reached that calendar day; the cap persists across reloads via localStorage.

StatsPanel shows an accessible heart gauge near the fullness gauge: heart icon + 'なつき度'/'Affection' label + bar + numeric value + band label, with an aria-label that conveys the value and band (not color-only).

Chat replies vary tone by affection band: warm => warmer/more familiar, cold => more distant, neutral keeps the current JA prompt byte-identical; JA and EN both implemented; baby stage still returns the canned non-verbal reply without calling Bedrock.
Chatting raises affection by AFFECTION_GAIN_CHAT (non-baby only) and a battle win raises it by AFFECTION_GAIN_BATTLE_WIN (persisted by the backend battle handler).
Legacy saves with no affection load fine (no validateMonster rejection) and show AFFECTION_INITIAL via normalizeAffection.
All new i18n keys exist in BOTH ja and en; existing JA/EN strings are unchanged.
New heart FX respects prefers-reduced-motion; no new runtime dependencies; audio-free.
`npm run build` is clean; `npm test` (shared) and the frontend helper test both pass with counts >= their post-FEAT-001 baselines.
verification: git diff --stat to confirm no package.json runtime dependency additions.
